speaker: m_ana
text: It's my mom, Carmen. She's 78 and lives on her own in Queens. I'm scared about three things. She gets her pills mixed up. Last week someone called her pretending to be my brother Marco and she almost sent him money. And last Thursday nobody went to see her, because Marco and I each thought the other one was going.

speaker: m_ana
text: Just the three of us. Marco's in Astoria, ten minutes from her. I'm in Brooklyn, about forty. Our sister Lucía is in New Jersey, she can't get there fast but she does the refills and all the insurance calls.
asked: I'm sorry, Ana. Let's start with the people. Who else is in this besides you and Marco, and how far is each of you from her?

speaker: m_ana
text: He works nights. Sunday through Thursday he has to leave the house by 9:30. He can do Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday evenings. He forgets, so he wants a text around 3 on his days.
asked: Marco first, since he's closest. What's his week like? When can he actually be there?

speaker: m_ana
text: Monday, Wednesday and Sunday, after four. I do all the doctor visits. Sunday lunch is at Mom's, and I fill her pill organizer while I'm there.
asked: And you? Which nights are yours, and what do you already do for her?

speaker: m_ana
text: Eliquis morning and night. Lisinopril in the morning, and Dr. Park just doubled that to 10 mg on the 3rd. Metformin twice a day. Atorvastatin at night. The old 5 mg lisinopril bottle is still in her cabinet. That one scares me.
asked: Her pills. What does she take, and who prescribed them?

speaker: m_ana
text: A weekly organizer. Yellow lid is morning, blue lid is evening. Two or three nights a week she calls me asking if she already took them. Once she took them twice.
asked: How does she take them day to day, and what happens on the nights she isn't sure?

speaker: m_ana
text: A man called saying he was Marco. Crying, in trouble, he needed $1,500 in gift cards right away. She was on her way to the store when she called me. Marco is the one who handles her money with her.
asked: Thank you. Now the money. Tell me about the call last week.

speaker: m_ana
text: Pavo. Thanksgiving is always at her place and Marco always brings the turkey.
asked: Pick a word only the family knows. Every real call from Village says it, so a caller without it is not us.

speaker: m_ana
text: Breakfast at eight with the morning pills. Blood pressure Monday, Wednesday, Friday, she writes it on a pad. Walk to the bakery at eleven with Doña Rosa, her neighbor on the third floor. Dinner at seven with her telenovela, evening pills at seven-thirty. It's a second-floor walk-up, no elevator; the super is Luis.
asked: Her day and her home: what does a normal day look like, and is anyone nearby?

speaker: m_ana
text: 911 first. Then me, then Marco. Elmhurst Hospital, it's the closest.
asked: If she falls or can't breathe, who is first?

speaker: m_ana
text: Spanish only. A regular phone, she won't use apps. If there's anything on a screen it has to be big letters. She'll answer a call. She won't read a text.
asked: And your mom herself. What language, what phone, and what will she actually use?

speaker: m_ana
text: After lunch, around 1:30. And please, no calls at night, she hates that.
asked: Two things Village can't take from you: Lucía's own yes to being called, and your mom's rules. Village asks Lucía in her app and calls your mom in Spanish to introduce itself. She can say no to all of it. When is she sharpest?

speaker: m_ana
text: Lucía should see the refill list too, she does the ordering.
asked: Here is the draft: four people, three life areas, five needs, ten rules on, one thing pending your mom. What is wrong?
